<a id="why_the_trapezoid_rule_on_sorted_nodes_has_no_n_to_the_minus_four_bound_for_log_zeta"></a>

### The integrand of the Cauchy average of log of zeta is not C^1 on the unit interval, so the N to the minus four bound of Yakowitz, Krimmel and Szidarovszky does not apply

Proposition 35.6.4, page 1247 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\frac12\le\theta<1$, $f(\tau)=\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau)|$ and $g=f\circ\tau$ with $\tau(u)=t_0+(1-\theta)\tan(\pi(u-\frac12))$, $u\in(0,1)$. If $\theta=\frac12$, $g$ is unbounded near $\tau^{-1}(\gamma)$ for every ordinate $\gamma$ of a zero on the line. If $\frac12<\theta<1$, $g'$ is unbounded near $u=0$ and near $u=1$. In both cases $g\notin C^1[0,1]$, so the bound $\mathbb{E}(T_N-\mathbb{E}_Pf)^2=O(N^{-4})$ of Yakowitz, Krimmel and Szidarovszky (1978) for the sorted trapezoid rule $T_N$ with $N$ uniform nodes, which assumes $g\in C^2[0,1]$, does not apply. The proof for $\frac12<\theta<1$ uses the mean value theorems $T^{-1}\int_1^T|\zeta(\theta+it)|^2dt\to\zeta(2\theta)$ and $T^{-1}\int_1^T|\zeta(\theta+it)|^4dt\to\zeta(2\theta)^4/\zeta(4\theta)$ and the inequality $\zeta(4\theta)<\zeta(2\theta)^2$.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:prop:rate`.

<a id="balazard_saias_yor_identity_on_a_half_disc_with_green_function_and_harmonic_measure"></a>

### The Balazard, Saias and Yor identity on a half disc: exact local form with the Green function of the half disc and zeros on the diameter subtracted

Theorem 35.6.6, page 1249 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $c=\theta+it_0$, $R>0$, $H=\{|s-c|<R,\operatorname{Re}s>\theta\}$, $z\in H$ and $\omega_z$ the harmonic measure of $\partial H$ seen from $z$. Let $h\not\equiv0$ be analytic on a neighbourhood of $\overline H$, with no zero on the closed arc $\{|s-c|=R,\operatorname{Re}s\ge\theta\}$, with zeros $\rho_1,\dots,\rho_n$ of multiplicities $m_1,\dots,m_n$ on the open diameter, and $h(z)\ne0$. Then $\int_{\partial H}(\log|h|-\sum_jm_j\log|s-\rho_j|)\,d\omega_z=\log|h(z)|-\sum_jm_j\log|z-\rho_j|+\sum_{\rho\in H}G_H(z,\rho)$, the last sum over the zeros of $h$ in $H$ with multiplicity, and the integrand on the left is real analytic on each of the two closed pieces of $\partial H$. In the coordinate $w=(s-c)/R$ with $w_z=(z-c)/R$, $w^*=-\overline{w_z}$ and $G_D(a,w)=\log|(1-\bar aw)/(w-a)|$, the Green function is $G_H(z,\cdot)=G_D(w_z,\cdot)-G_D(w^*,\cdot)$; on the arc $w=e^{i\phi}$, $|\phi|\le\frac\pi2$, the harmonic measure has density $\frac{1-|w_z|^2}{2\pi|e^{i\phi}-w_z|^2}-\frac{1-|w^*|^2}{2\pi|e^{i\phi}-w^*|^2}$ with respect to $d\phi$, and on the diameter $w=iy$ the density with respect to $dy$ is $\frac1{2\pi}\partial_x[G_D(w_z,x+iy)-G_D(w^*,x+iy)]$ at $x=0$. Both densities are real analytic up to the corners $w=\pm i$, where they vanish to first order. In particular $h$ has no zero in $H$ if and only if the identity holds without the Green sum.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:thm:halfdisk`.

<a id="half_disc_identity_tends_to_the_balazard_saias_yor_identity_as_the_radius_tends_to_infinity"></a>

### The half disc identity becomes the Balazard, Saias and Yor identity on the half plane as the radius tends to infinity

Remark 35.6.7, page 1250 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $h_\theta(s)=\zeta(s)\frac{s-1}{s-2\theta+1}$ and $z=1+it_0$. Along radii $R_k\to\infty$ with $|t_0\pm R_k-\gamma|\ge c/\log R_k$ for every zero ordinate $\gamma$, the arc term of the half disc identity tends to $0$ (on the arc the density is at most $CR^{-1}\cos\phi$, so the part of the arc with $\theta\le\operatorname{Re}s\le2$ has harmonic measure $O(R_k^{-3})$, and there $|\log|h_\theta||=O(\log^2R_k)$, while $|\log|h_\theta(s)||=O(2^{-\operatorname{Re}s}+R_k^{-1})$ on the rest of the arc), the density on the diameter increases to the Cauchy density of scale $1-\theta$ and centre $t_0$, and the Green sum increases to the sum of the Green potentials of the zeros right of the line. So the half disc identity becomes the Balazard, Saias and Yor identity at $1+it_0$. That the arc carries vanishing harmonic measure would not suffice by itself: for $h(s)=e^{s-\theta}$ the arc contributes $1-\theta$ for every $R$.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:rem:halfplane`.

<a id="exact_bias_and_variance_of_the_sorted_trapezoid_rule_at_independent_uniform_nodes"></a>

### The sorted trapezoid rule at independent uniform nodes: exact leading bias and variance of order N to the minus five, so mean square N to the minus four, and N to the minus five when the end slopes agree

Lemma 35.6.8, page 1250 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $g\in C^4[a,b]$ and let $T_N$ be the trapezoid rule on the sorted $N$ independent uniform nodes on $[a,b]$ with the end points $a$ and $b$ added. Then $\mathbb{E}T_N-\int_a^bg=\frac{(b-a)^2(g'(b)-g'(a))}{2(N+1)(N+2)}+O(N^{-3})$ and $\operatorname{Var}T_N=O(N^{-5})$. So the mean square error is $O(N^{-4})$, and $O(N^{-5})$ when $g'(a)=g'(b)$.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:lem:trap`.

<a id="half_disc_boundary_integral_by_sorted_trapezoid_rule_has_mean_square_rate_n_to_the_minus_four_and_minus_five"></a>

### Half disc identity: the sorted trapezoid rule on the two smooth pieces of the boundary has mean square error O(N^-4), and O(N^-5) after a change of variable

Result 35.6.5, page 1251 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. In the half disc identity, each of the two pieces of the boundary integral is a smooth integrand on a closed interval vanishing at the ends. By the sorted trapezoid rule lemma the rule with $N/2$ nodes on each piece has mean square error $O(N^{-4})$, its bias $\frac{2(b-a)^2(g'(b)-g'(a))}{(N+2)(N+4)}+O(N^{-3})$ vanishing to that order only if the end slopes agree. The change of variable $y=\Phi(v)=v+\sin(\pi v)/\pi$ on each piece, written on $[-1,1]$, makes the transformed integrand $g(\Phi(v))\Phi'(v)$ vanish to at least fifth order at the ends, since $\Phi'(\pm(1-r))=\frac{\pi^2}2r^2+O(r^4)$ and $1-|\Phi(\pm(1-r))|=\frac{\pi^2}6r^3+O(r^5)$; both end slopes are then zero and the mean square error is $O(N^{-5})$. These are upper bounds.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:res:halfdisk_rates`.

<a id="tail_of_the_cauchy_average_of_log_zeta_beyond_height_t_under_rh"></a>

### Under RH, the Cauchy tail of log of zeta beyond distance T from the centre is O(log T / (T^2 (log log T)^2)) at level one half and O(T^-2 log T) at levels above

Result 35.6.6, page 1252 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on The Riemann hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part 1/2.

Statement. Assume the Riemann hypothesis. Let $t_0\in\mathbb{R}$ and $P_{1/2}(t_0-\tau)$ the Cauchy density of centre $t_0$ and scale $\frac12$. Using the estimate $\int_T^t\log|\zeta(\frac12+iu)|\,du=O(\log t/(\log\log t)^2)$ for $3\le T\le t$ (Bui, Lester and Milinovich 2014) and integration by parts, $\int_{|\tau-t_0|>T}\log|\zeta(\frac12+i\tau)|\,P_{1/2}(t_0-\tau)\,d\tau=O_{t_0}(\log T/(T^2(\log\log T)^2))$. At a level $\theta\in(\frac12,1)$, under the same hypothesis, the integral of $\log\zeta$ around the rectangle with vertices $\theta+iT$, $\theta+it$ and $+\infty$ bounds the primitive of $\log|\zeta(\theta+iu)|$ by $O_\theta(\log t)$, and the tail of the Cauchy average (scale $1-\theta$) beyond $T$ by $O_\theta(T^{-2}\log T)$. The case $t_0=0$, $\theta=\frac12$ is a theorem of Bui, Lester and Milinovich; the extension to every centre and to the levels above one half is the book's.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:res:tail`.

<a id="computed_truncation_error_of_the_cauchy_average_by_the_shifted_trapezoid_rule_on_the_whole_line"></a>

### Computed errors of the truncated shifted trapezoid rule for the Cauchy average of log of zeta over a window at height 85.7, with zeros deflated at level one half

Table 35.6, page 1253 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Computed in floating point at $t_0=85.7$: the error of the shifted trapezoid rule for the Cauchy average of $\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau)|$ over $|\tau-t_0|\le T$, minus $\log|h_\theta(1+it_0)|$, mean over $10$ random shifts. At $\theta=\frac34$ (step $0.02$): errors $-9.47\times10^{-4}$, $-3.40\times10^{-5}$, $+4.36\times10^{-6}$, $+6.47\times10^{-8}$, $-1.36\times10^{-7}$ at $T=10,40,160,640,1280$. At $\theta=\frac12$ (step $0.01$, the zeros with $|\gamma-t_0|\le T+1$ deflated and their window means added back): $-2.09\times10^{-3}$, $-5.37\times10^{-5}$, $+1.05\times10^{-5}$, $+7.84\times10^{-8}$ at $T=10,40,160,640$, with $10,33,123,742$ zeros deflated. The shifted grid is unbiased for the window integral, so the mean error is minus the Cauchy tail. This is a computation and not a theorem about the rule: at a fixed step the discretisation error of one shift need not tend to $0$ as $T$ grows, and the bounds on the tail are conditional on the Riemann hypothesis. Adding back the whole line means of the deflating functions instead would add their tails, and for that variant $T^2\cdot|\mathrm{error}|$ grows from $0.15$ at $T=10$ to $1.24$ at $T=640$ (computed).

<a id="rates_of_the_shifted_trapezoid_grid_for_the_smoothed_riesz_integrand"></a>

### Rates of the randomly shifted product trapezoid rule on the torus (every power for a smooth periodic integrand, order N to the minus one with a logarithmic singularity) and N to the minus three halves for Voronoi and Delaunay weights at independent uniform nodes

Proposition 35.7.2, page 1256 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $g$ be square integrable on the torus $[0,1)^2$ and $Q(\delta)=m^{-2}\sum_{j\in\{0,\dots,m-1\}^2}g(j/m+\delta)$, with $N=m^2$ nodes and $\delta$ uniform on $[0,1/m)^2$. Then $\mathbb{E}_\delta Q=\int g$ and $\mathbb{E}_\delta|Q-\int g|^2=\sum_{\ell\ne0}|\hat g(m\ell)|^2$. (i) If $g$ has a smooth periodic extension, for example $g=\log|f|\,\Delta\varphi$ with $\varphi$ the flat bump $b(x)b(y)$, $b(x)=e^{-1/(1-x^2)}$, and $f$ without zeros in the box, then $Q(\delta)-\int g=O(N^{-k})$ for every $k$, uniformly in $\delta$. (ii) If $g=\psi\log|s-\rho|$ with $\psi\in C_c^\infty((0,1)^2)$ and $\rho\in(0,1)^2$, then $(\mathbb{E}_\delta|Q-\int g|^2)^{1/2}=O(N^{-1})$; for a fixed shift whose nodes all lie at distance at least $c/m$ from $\rho$, $|Q-\int g|=O_c(N^{-1}\log N)$; and if $\psi(\rho)\ne0$ no bound uniform in the shift holds. (iii) On the box, for $g\in C^3$ with $g=0$ near the boundary, or $g$ smooth with every derivative vanishing on the boundary (for example $g=\log|f|\,\Delta\varphi$ when $f$ has no zero in the closed box), Voronoi weights (cells clipped to the box) and Delaunay weights (triangulation of the nodes and the four corners of the box) at independent uniform nodes have root mean square error $O(N^{-3/2})$, against $N^{-1/2}$ for the sample mean; this is proved by the weighted Monte Carlo theorem with $d=2$. At jittered nodes the same rate is computed, not proved. The variance identity and part (i) are standard for randomly shifted lattice rules; parts (ii) and (iii) are the book's.

Source: [`ch/bsy3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy3.tex), label `bsy:prop:rates2d`.

<a id="weighted_monte_carlo_voronoi_and_delaunay_rules_at_independent_uniform_nodes_have_rate_n_to_the_minus_one_half_minus_two_over_d"></a>

### Voronoi and Delaunay weighted Monte Carlo at independent uniform nodes for integrands flat at the boundary: root mean square error O(N^(-1/2-2/d)) in every dimension d

Theorem 35.7.3, page 1257 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $Q=[-1,1]^d$, $X_1,\dots,X_N$ independent and uniform on $Q$, and $g\in C^3(Q)$ with (a) $g=0$ within distance $\delta>0$ of $\partial Q$, or (b) $g\in C^\infty(Q)$ with every derivative vanishing on $\partial Q$. Let $V_N=\sum_i|V_i\cap Q|\,g(X_i)$ be the Voronoi rule with the cells clipped to $Q$, $D_N=\int_QI_Ng$ the Delaunay rule, where $I_Ng$ interpolates $g$ linearly on the Delaunay triangulation of the nodes and the $2^d$ corners of $Q$. With $d(x)$ the distance from $x$ to the nearest node and $v(x)$ the vector from $x$ to it, $V_N-\int_Qg=\frac12\int_Qd^2\,\Delta g\,dx+\frac12\int_Qv^{\mathsf T}D^2g\,v\,dx+\int_Qr\,dx$ with $|r(x)|\le\frac16\|D^3g\|_\infty|v|^3$. For $A_N=V_N$ and for $A_N=D_N$, $|\mathbb{E}A_N-\int_Qg|=O(Ne^{-cN\delta^d})$ in case (a) and $O(N^{-k})$ for every $k$ in case (b), and $\operatorname{Var}A_N=O(N^{-1-4/d})$. So the root mean square error is $O(N^{-1/2-2/d})$ in every dimension, with constants depending on $g$, $d$ and, in case (a), $\delta$. Case (b) includes $g=\log|f|\,\Delta\varphi$ for the flat bump $\varphi$ of the smoothed Riesz identity mapped to $Q$, when $f$ is analytic and zero free on a neighbourhood of the closed box.

Source: [`ch/bsy3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy3.tex), label `bsy:thm:wmc`.

<a id="computed_errors_of_weighted_rules_at_independent_uniform_nodes_in_one_and_two_dimensions"></a>

### Computed root mean square errors of the Voronoi, Delaunay and trapezoid rules at independent uniform nodes for flat and non flat integrands in one and two dimensions

Table 35.7, page 1259 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Computed in floating point, root mean square error at independent uniform nodes on $[-1,1]^d$ at $N=1000$ and at the largest $N=1{,}024{,}000$, slopes fitted for $N\ge4000$, over $200$ replications in one dimension and $30$ in two (about $5$ percent noise in one dimension and about $13$ percent in two). Bump $\prod_ib(x_i/0.9)$, $d=1$, Voronoi: $1.2\times10^{-6}$ and $3.5\times10^{-14}$, slope $-2.51$. $e^x$, $d=1$, sorted trapezoid: $4.8\times10^{-6}$ and $4.5\times10^{-12}$, slope $-2.00$. Bump, $d=2$, Voronoi: $1.4\times10^{-4}$ and $5.1\times10^{-9}$, slope $-1.46$. Bump, $d=2$, Delaunay: $1.1\times10^{-4}$ and $4.2\times10^{-9}$, slope $-1.42$. $e^{x+y/2}$, $d=2$, Delaunay: $1.0\times10^{-2}$ and $1.2\times10^{-5}$, slope $-0.98$. The slopes are consistent with the exponents $-\frac52$ and $-\frac32$ of the weighted Monte Carlo theorem for the bump, with $-2$ of the sorted trapezoid rule lemma for $e^x$, and with a bias of order $N^{-2/d}$ for the exponentials, which do not vanish at the boundary. This is a computation and not a proof.

Source: [`ch/bsy3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy3.tex), label `bsy:tab:wmc`.

<a id="approximate_deflation_of_a_zero_leaves_no_floor_for_the_shifted_trapezoid_grid"></a>

### Approximate deflation: the shifted trapezoid grid error with a zero estimate at distance epsilon has two regimes and no floor

Proposition 35.7.5, page 1262 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\psi\in C_c^\infty((0,1)^2)$, $\rho,\hat\rho\in(0,1)^2$ with $0<\varepsilon=|\hat\rho-\rho|\le\frac12$ and $r=\psi\,(\log|s-\rho|-\log|s-\hat\rho|)$. The randomly shifted product trapezoid rule with $N$ nodes is unbiased for $\int r$, and its root mean square error over the shift is at most $C\bigl(\varepsilon N^{-1/2}(1+\log^+\frac1{\varepsilon\sqrt N})^{1/2}+\varepsilon\log\frac2\varepsilon\,N^{-1}\bigr)$ if $\varepsilon\sqrt N\le1$ and $C\,N^{-1}$ if $\varepsilon\sqrt N\ge1$, with $C$ depending only on $\psi$. So for every fixed $\varepsilon$ the error tends to zero.

Source: [`ch/bsy3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy3.tex), label `bsy:prop:defl`.

<a id="counting_zeros_from_the_horizontal_logarithmic_derivative_alone"></a>

### The zero count weighted by a bump is a linear functional of the horizontal logarithmic derivative on a half strip

Theorem 35.7.6, page 1262 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $f\not\equiv0$ be meromorphic on a connected neighbourhood of $\{\operatorname{Re}s\ge\sigma_0\}$ and equal, for $\operatorname{Re}s$ large, to an absolutely convergent Dirichlet series $1+\sum_{n\ge2}a_nn^{-s}$, such as $\zeta$ or the Davenport and Heilbronn function. Let $d_f(u,t)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)(u+it)$, $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\{\operatorname{Re}s>\sigma_0\})$, $\Phi(u,t)=\int_{-\infty}^u\varphi(\sigma,t)\,d\sigma$ and $K_\varphi=\partial_u\varphi+\partial_t^2\Phi$. Then $\sum_{f(\rho)=0}\varphi(\rho)-\sum_{f(p)=\infty}\varphi(p)=-\frac12\int_{-\infty}^\infty\int_{\sigma_0}^\infty d_f(u,t)\,K_\varphi(u,t)\,du\,dt$, with zeros and poles counted with multiplicity and the double integral absolutely convergent. $K_\varphi$ is smooth, and to the right of the support of $\varphi$ it equals $\partial_t^2\Phi(\infty,t)$ and does not depend on $u$.

Source: [`ch/bsy3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy3.tex), label `bsy:thm:thorincount`.

<a id="computed_error_of_the_deflated_shifted_grid_against_the_error_of_the_deflating_zero"></a>

### Computed error of the deflated shifted grid for the Davenport and Heilbronn function as a function of the error in the deflating zero

Table 35.9, page 1263 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

<a id="explicit_formula_at_a_cauchy_smoothed_level_gives_the_thorin_integral_when_no_zero_lies_right_of_the_level"></a>

### The explicit formula at a Cauchy smoothed level: the primes compute the Thorin integral against a band limited test function only when no zero lies to the right of the level

Remark 35.8.1, page 1265 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $F\ge0$ have a Fourier transform supported in $[-L,L]$, Lipschitz with derivative of bounded variation, $F_c=F(\cdot-c)$, and $\frac12<\sigma<1$ not the real part of a zero (otherwise take right limits in $\sigma$). The explicit formula of Weil applied to the even part of $P_{\sigma-1/2}*F_c$, with $P$ the Cauchy density, has on its prime side only the prime powers $n\le e^L$, besides the archimedean terms. On its zero side a zero $\beta+i\gamma$ with $\beta<\sigma$ contributes $\int F_c\,P_{\sigma-\beta}(\cdot-\gamma)$, its term in $\int F_c\,d\mathfrak U_\sigma$, where $\mathfrak U_\sigma$ is the Thorin measure at level $\sigma$. So if no zero has $\beta>\sigma$ the formula gives $\int F_c\,d\mathfrak U_\sigma\ge0$. A zero with $\beta>\sigma$ contributes the continuation in $\beta$ of that term, which exceeds its signed term $-\int F_c\,P_{\beta-\sigma}(\cdot-\gamma)$ in $\int F_c\,d\mathfrak U_\sigma$ by $F_c(\gamma+i(\beta-\sigma))+F_c(\gamma-i(\beta-\sigma))$; these corrections need not be positive. So the primes compute the continued Weil functional, which equals the Thorin integral in general only when no zero lies to the right of $\sigma$.

Source: [`ch/bsy3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy3.tex), label `bsy:rem:weil`.

<a id="open_implementable_sampler_with_variance_below_plain_monte_carlo_for_the_defect"></a>

### Open problem: an implementable sampler whose variance per unit cost for the defect is below plain Monte Carlo

Problem 35.1, page 1265 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Let $\frac12\le\theta<1$, $t_0\in\mathbb{R}$, $f(\tau)=\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau)|$, $P$ the Cauchy law with density $\frac{1-\theta}{\pi((1-\theta)^2+(t_0-\tau)^2)}$, $h_\theta(s)=\zeta(s)\frac{s-1}{s-2\theta+1}$ and $D_\theta(t_0)=\mathbb{E}_Pf-\log|h_\theta(1+it_0)|$. Find an implementable sampler for the law $P_w\propto P\,w(f)$ with $w$ close to $|f-\mathbb{E}_Pf|$, or another weight, whose variance per unit of computing cost (pilot, burn in, autocorrelation and evaluations of $f$ included) is below that of plain Monte Carlo for the defect $D_\theta(t_0)$, or show that the Metropolis chains of the chapter cannot reach it. For independent draws no weight gains more than the factor $\mathrm{Var}_Pf/(\mathbb{E}_P|f-\mathbb{E}_Pf|)^2$, which is between $1.35$ and $2.46$ for the nine integrands of the book's table of defects (computed); a Markov chain is not bound by it.

### Open problem: the root mean square rate of Voronoi and Delaunay rules for the negative Thorin mass on a region free of zeros

Problem 35.2, page 1265 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

### Open problem: extend the rate of Voronoi and Delaunay weights to dependent nodes and find the rate for a box with an undeflated zero

<a id="open_converse_of_the_moment_identities_and_the_central_limit_theorem_for_log_h_theta"></a>

### Open problem: do the moment identities for all heights imply QRH(theta), and a central limit theorem for the logarithm of h under the Cauchy law

Problem 35.5, page 1266 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Fix $\theta\in[\frac12,1)$ and let $Z_{t_0}$ be the boundary value of the branch of $\log h_\theta$, $h_\theta(s)=\zeta(s)\frac{s-1}{s-2\theta+1}$, continued horizontally from $+\infty$, at a height with the Cauchy law of centre $t_0$ and scale $1-\theta$. If $\mathbb{E}[Z_{t_0}^2]=(\mathbb{E}Z_{t_0})^2$ for every $t_0$, does $\mathrm{QRH}(\theta)$ follow? By the cut formula for complex moments this is equivalent to the identity $2\sum_\gamma\int_{C_\gamma}M_\gamma(L_-+\pi iM_\gamma-z_0)K\,ds=D^2$ for every $t_0$, over the horizontal cuts $C_\gamma$ from the zeros right of the line to the line, with $M_\gamma$ the number of zeros on the cut to the right of the point, $L_-$ the boundary value of the logarithm from below, $z_0=\log h_\theta(1+it_0)$, $K$ the kernel $\frac1{s-z^*}-\frac1{s-z}$ with $z=1+it_0$, $z^*=2\theta-1+it_0$, and $D=\mathbb{E}Z_{t_0}-z_0$. Under the Riemann hypothesis, is $\operatorname{Var}\log|\zeta(\frac12+i\tau)|=\frac12\log\log t_0+O(1)$ under the Cauchy law of centre $t_0$ and scale $\frac12$, for every $t_0$ or for $t_0$ outside a set of density zero; and does $(Z_{t_0}-\mathbb{E}Z_{t_0})/(\frac12\log\log t_0)^{1/2}$ converge in law to the standard normal law of $\mathbb{R}^2$ when $t_0$ is uniform on $[T,2T]$?

<a id="open_negative_trace_for_a_combination_of_primitive_l_functions"></a>

### Open problem: a combination of L functions of primitive characters of one modulus, with a functional equation and zeros off the line, whose trace is negative somewhere

Problem 35.6, page 1266 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Is there a linear combination of $L(s,\chi)$ over primitive characters $\chi$ of one modulus, with a functional equation and zeros off the line, whose trace $K(u)=\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{-\gamma|u|}\cos((\beta-\frac12)u)$ over its zeros $\beta+i\gamma$ is negative for some $u$? With imprimitive characters allowed, a real combination of $L$ functions of characters modulo $4$, $4p$, $4q$ and $4pq$ gives one. If the lowest zero $\frac12+i\gamma_1$ of such a function is on the line, the argument of the book's proof for the Davenport and Heilbronn function gives a positive trace whenever $\sum e^{-(\gamma-\gamma_1)\pi/(2\delta_{\max})}<1$, the sum over the upper zeros off the line with multiplicity and $\delta_{\max}$ the largest $|\beta-\frac12|$; so a negative trace needs the opposite inequality, and if there are finitely many, $M$, upper zeros off the line, one of them lies within $\frac{2\delta_{\max}}\pi\log M$ of $\gamma_1$.

# P = RP <small>A Monte Carlo Program for P versus NP</small>

By Nick Polson and [Vadim Sokolov](https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6618-2965).

[![PDF](https://vsokolov.org/books/icon-pdf.svg)](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/p_equals_rp/releases/download/v1.0.0/p_equals_rp.pdf "PDF") [![Source on GitHub](https://vsokolov.org/books/icon-github.svg)](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/p_equals_rp/tree/v1.0.0 "Source on GitHub") [![DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23738431](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.23738431.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23738431)

## Description

Counting the solutions of the N queens problem is a rare event probability, and a rare event probability is the integral of a quantile function on the unit interval: the Lorenz curve identity behind nested sampling and vertical likelihood Monte Carlo. This book turns that observation into a Monte Carlo program for the P versus NP problem, stated as a sequence of theorems and conjectures with the gaps marked.

Part I sets out the problem from Hilbert, Turing and Shannon to the randomized classes RP and BPP, the barriers, the exponential time hypothesis, Kolmogorov complexity and pseudorandomness. Part II is the queens: Gauss and Nauck, the rare event reformulation, Simkin's queenon, entropy and rate functions. Part III develops the machinery: product estimators, mixing times, cross entropy, Lorenz curves, vertical likelihood and its Yakowitz type error bounds, nested sampling, sequential Monte Carlo and generative Bayesian computation.

Part IV states the program. The sampling half proves that NP = RP is equivalent to polynomial time sampling and approximate counting of the completions of partial queens boards, and states as conjectures the mixing conditions under which a vertical walk on the energy levels would deliver them. The derandomization half, which gives the book its title, restates promise RP = promise P, which implies P = RP, as the known hitting set problem on the quantile axis and does not claim a proof. The book reports exact computations on the queens: the density of states, the giant component of solutions on conditioned boards, the shattering depth of the bottom level sets, and spectral gaps, all reproducible from the code in its repository, and ends with the open problems and their status.

## Main results

- [Coding theorem for the queens](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#coding_theorem_for_the_queens) (Theorem 12.1, page 47): NP equals RP exactly when the completions of every queens board can be encoded and decoded in randomized polynomial time at their information content, the logarithm of the completion count up to a logarithmic term.
- [Product proposals for the queens](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#product_proposals_for_the_queens) (Theorem 30.1, page 116): No importance sampling proposal with independent coordinates can beat crude Monte Carlo for counting N queens by more than a factor given by the entropy deficit of the solution marginals, which is small for N up to 12.
- [Trapezoid on random nodes for bounded variation, no logarithm](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#trapezoid_bounded_variation_no_log) (Theorem 37.4, page 151): For any integrand of bounded variation V the trapezoid on random ordered nodes has bias at most V over 2(n+1) and mean squared error at most V squared over 2(n+1)(n+2), with no logarithm and no dependence on the number of steps.
- [Learning the posterior mean matrix is equivalent to NP equals RP](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#learning_problem_equivalent_to_np_rp) (Theorem 42.7, page 181): NP equals RP is equivalent to a randomized polynomial time algorithm, or a uniform polynomial size circuit family, computing the queens posterior mean matrix of every board to relative accuracy one over N squared.
- [The main equivalence, NP = RP if and only if queens completions can be sampled or counted in polynomial time](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#main_equivalence_np_rp_queens_sampling) (Theorem 58.1, page 242): NP equals RP exactly when the completions of a partial queens placement can be sampled almost uniformly, the level sets of the queens energy can be sampled, or the number of completions can be approximated, in randomized polynomial time.
- [Conditional FPRAS for the vertical walk with stratified quadrature](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#conditional_fpras_vertical_walk) (Theorem 43.1, page 185): Given a level set sampler and a ladder of at most 2K rungs with ratios at least one half, the vertical walk with stratified quadrature approximates the ground state count in time K squared over epsilon squared times the sampler cost, so counting reduces to level set sampling. Status: conditional on a level set sampler producing, in time C(N, delta), a sample within total variation delta of uniform on every sublevel set; the ladder hypothesis, that the ladder has at most 2K rungs and consecutive rung size ratios at least one half; for the optimality remark only, for the optimality remark only, that relative error epsilon in the product requires relative error of order epsilon over the square root of K in each rung ratio, which the book assumes and does not prove.
- [Expansion of the bottom level set is equivalent to polynomial mixing](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#expansion_equivalent_to_mixing) (Theorem 56.5, page 237): By Cheeger's inequality, a polynomial lower bound on the conductance of the giant component gives polynomial mixing of the lazy swap chain, and polynomial mixing conversely gives the conductance bound.

All 47 results of the book (31 proved, 7 conditional, 9 open) are on the page [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html), each with its statement, status and number.
